title: Halting After a Clean Call
statement: Let $C$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, with designated entry and exit states, and let $x$, $\mathrm{arg}$, $\mathrm{result}$, and $\mathrm{out}$ be Boolean words. Starting from the configuration on input $x$ with entry state and tape contents given by the state word of $\mathrm{arg}$, suppose $t>0$, the machine's state is not the exit state at any time $v$ with $0<v<t$, and at time $t$ it is in the configuration with exit state, tape contents given by the state word of $\mathrm{result}$, and output $\mathrm{out}$. Then the call-stopping wrapper, started on input $x$ with release flag down, entry state, and tape contents given by the state word of $\mathrm{arg}$, reaches after $t+1$ steps a halted configuration with release flag raised, exit state, tape contents given by the state word of $\mathrm{result}$, and output $\mathrm{out}$.
hypotheses_covered: The machine avoids the exit state at every time $v$ with $0<v<t$
At time $t$, the machine is in the specified exit configuration with output $\mathrm{out}$
replaced:
Let a machine $C$, started at its entry over the state word of an argument,
avoid its designated exit at all intermediate positive times before $t > 0$ and
reach at time $t$ the exit over the state word of a result with a given output.
Then the call-stopping wrapper, started with the flag down, runs for $t + 1$
steps and halts in that same physical configuration (flag raised, state halted),
retaining every emitted bit.
